The Illinois Pollution Control Board has designated the water quality for Thorn Creek and Butterfield Creek as general use.
Exhibits "15" to "20" on the following pages were taken from the Water Quality Network, 1973 Summary of Data, Volume 3 printed by the State of Illinois Environmental Protection Agency. This volume covers the Des Plaines River Basin. Exhibit "19" represents the summary of 1973 water quality data for Thorn Creek at Halsted Street in Chicago Heights and Exhibit "20" represents the summary of 1973 water quality data for Butterfield Creek at Crawford Avenue.
Oil spillage resulting from vehicles is generally restricted to the riding surface. Because concrete is porous, spillage is normally absorbed within the concrete and the sub-base.
In the event of the overturning of a carrier, the maintenance crew would utilize sand to absorb the oil. The saturated material is then disposed of in accordance with the State Environmental Protection Agency "Rules and Regulations."
Special care will be taken to prevent, control, and remove any spillage of oils, fuels or any potentially polluted material during the construction of Lincoln Highway.
The contractors will be responsible for the area of raw, erodible earth exposed at any given time. Since the proposed improvement consists only of widening and reconstruction, erosion and sedimentation should be minimal (See Appendix D).
